header.author: Book of the Dead
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:tb:pkairo-cg-24095-pmaiherperi:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.125.1: 125.1: the editor reads sw 'him' from the scribe's nswt. 125.5: zꜣwt=s, 'its guarding' or 'its wardens', is obscure; mdwt 'words' (or 'affairs') in 'reckoning of words'.
notes.125.53: Several names and offences are uncertain. 125.59: ḫbjt, 'deduction', taken as cheating. 125.62: wḏ ns, 'who sends the tongue'; ns may stand for nsr 'flame'. 125.63: knj not understood. 125.64: ṯhm perhaps 'trespass, encroach'. 125.66: ḥnwyt not understood. 125.67: ḥnt taken as 'rations'. 125.69: the name ꜥꜣ-wdy is not understood; šm-rʾ, 'going of the mouth', taken as babbling. 125.72: dꜣdꜣ taken as 'fornicate'. 125.79: nwḥ not understood. 125.80: the sense of nkk, the partner, is disputed. 125.81: 'swallowed my heart' (ꜥm-jb) may mean being impatient or hiding resentment. 125.85: jwn, 'colour, nature'; sense unclear. 125.86: jꜥ[r] is restored by the editor; 'approach' is a guess. 125.90: the name tm-zp is not understood. 125.94: nḥbt is 'neck' or 'lotus bud'. 125.97: sꜣt taken as 'slight, despise'. nʾt is taken as 'the city'.
notes.125.143: 125.145: wšn may be the verb 'wring (a bird's neck)' or a kind of bird. 125.146: ztj 'ochre, pigment'; sẖkr 'adorned, overlaid' is uncertain; mꜣj 'lion' is odd here and may be miswritten for another animal. 125.147 and 125.155: jrr is marked sic in the edition. 125.149: ḥntꜣ is not understood ('be in want'? 'be greedy'?).
notes.149.139: nꜥw is a serpent; nꜥw pw may mean 'I am the nꜥw-serpent' or 'it is the nꜥw-serpent'. The editor deletes a t in nꜥw.

nodes.text: What is said on reaching the Broad Hall of the Two Truths, to separate him from the wrongdoing he has done, and to see the faces of the gods.
Hail to you, great god, lord of the Two Truths!
I have come to you, my lord, having been brought
so that I may see your beauty.

I know your name, I know the names of the 42 gods who are with you in this Broad Hall of the Two Truths, who live on its guarding(?), who swallow their blood on that day of the reckoning of words before Wennefer.
I have not turned cattle away from the god's property.
I have not opposed a god in his procession.
I am pure! Four times.
My purity (twice) is [that of] that great Benu-bird which is in Herakleopolis,

for I am that nose of the Lord of Breath, who keeps all the people alive, on that day of filling the wedjat-Eye in Heliopolis, in the second month of Peret, on the last day, in the presence of the lord of this land.
O Wide-of-Strides who came forth from Heliopolis, I have done no wrong.
O Embracer-of-Flame who came forth from Kheraha, I have not robbed.
O Nose who came forth from Hermopolis, I have not been greedy.
O Swallower-of-Shadows who came forth from the cavern, I have not stolen.
O Terrible-of-Face who came forth from Rosetau, I have not killed people.
O Double Lion who came forth from the sky, I have not damaged provisions.
O His-Eyes-are-Flint who came forth from Letopolis, I have not cheated(?).
O Flame who came forth backwards, I have not stolen the god's property.
O Bone-Breaker who came forth from Herakleopolis, I have not told lies.
O Sender-of-Flame(?) who came forth from Memphis, I have not taken away food.
O Cavern-Dweller who came forth from the West, I have not sulked(?).
O White-of-Teeth who came forth from the Fayum, I have not trespassed(?).
O Eater-of-Blood who came forth from the slaughter-place, I have not slaughtered the god's cattle.
O Eater-of-Entrails who came forth from the House of Thirty, I have not done *ḥnwyt*.
O Lord-of-Maat who came forth from Maaty, I have not robbed rations(?).
O Wanderer who came forth from Bubastis, I have not eavesdropped.
O *Aa-wedy* who came forth from Heliopolis, I have not babbled(?).
O Djudju who came forth from Andjet, I have not quarrelled except over my own property.
O Wamemty who came forth from the place of execution, I have not copulated with a married woman.
O He-who-Sees-what-He-has-Brought who came forth from the House of Min, I have not fornicated.
O Chief-of-the-Great-Ones who came forth from the acacia, I have not caused terror.
O Destroyer who came forth from the Great Seat, I have not transgressed.
O Maker-of-Uproar who came forth from Weryt, I have not been hot-tempered.
O Youth who came forth from Heqa-andj, I have not made myself deaf to words of truth.
O Announcer-of-Voice who came forth from Wenesy, I have not made trouble.
O Basty who came forth from the Secret Place, I have not caused weeping.
O His-Face-Behind-Him who came forth from the cave, I have not committed *nwḥ*.
I have not copulated with a catamite(?).
O Hot-of-Foot who came forth from the dusk, I have not swallowed my heart.
O Kenemty who came forth from Kenmet, I have not reviled.
O Bringer-of-his-Offering who came forth from Sais, I have not been violent.
O Lord-of-Faces who came forth from Nedjfet, I have not been hasty of heart.
O Counsellor who came forth from Wetjenet, I have not transgressed against *jwn*(?).
I have not [approached](?) a god.
O Two-Horned One who came forth from Asyut, I have not been loud of voice in speech.
O Nefertem who came forth from Memphis, I have no wrongdoing.
I have not done evil.
O *Temsep* who came forth from Busiris, I have not reviled the king.
O Who-Acts-by-his-Heart who came forth from Tjebu, I have not waded in water.
O Ihy who came forth from Nun, I have not raised my voice.
O Commander-of-the-People who came forth from his sanctuary, I have not reviled a god.
O Beautiful-Neck(?) who came forth from Gem-wesh, I have not been puffed up.
O Nehebkau who came forth from the city, I have not made distinctions for myself.
O Holy-of-Head who came forth from the city, my portion has not been great except through my own property.
O Bringer-of-his-Arm who came forth from the city, I have not slighted the god in my city.
Rescue me from Babi, who lives on the entrails of the great ones, on that day of the great reckoning.
You shall tell it to the Interpreter of the Two Lands.
Who is he?
The Interpreter of the Two Lands is Thoth.
Come, says Thoth.
Why have you come?
I have come to be announced.
What is your condition?
I am pure of wrongdoing;
I have protected myself from the quarrelling of those who are in their days;
I am not among them.
To whom, then, shall I announce you?
To him whose roof is fire, whose walls are living uraei,
and whose floor is water.
Who is he?
It is Osiris.
Proceed, then!
See, you are announced.
He shall purify himself,
having put on a pair of white sandals, anointed with the finest myrrh,
having offered cattle, wrung(?) fowl, incense, bread, beer and vegetables.
Now you shall make this image, which is in writing, on a clean floor, in clean ochre, overlaid(?) with earth on which no pig or lion(?) has trodden.
As for him over whom this book is made, he will flourish,
and his children's children will flourish.
He will not be in want(?).
He will be a confidant of the king and his entourage.
He will be given a *šns*-loaf, a *ds*-jug, a *psn*-cake and a large portion of meat on the altar of the great god.
He will not be held back at any gate of the West.
He will be ushered in with the kings of Upper and Lower Egypt.
He will be in the following of Osiris.
Truly correct, a million times; very effective for him who does it.
The way is cleared for me, that *nꜥw*-serpent, the bull of Nut, Nehebkau.
